Stupid fear mongering. According to Wolfram Alpha, the US currently has a population density of 91 people per square mile. That's rank 179 worldwide. It doesn't really matter how many people immigrate to the US, but who and how. There is so much space, even a population multiple times as high as now could easily be sustained. Also, there is not a fixed number of jobs to do, with more people there have to be more jobs, because the additional people create additional demand. So the key factor is how productive will the new immigrants be. There is basically no limit to the demand of highly productive and/or innovative workers, because they will increase the global competitiveness and create added value for everyone, thus raising the standard of living.

The problem are unproductive people who immediately or eventually become dependent of welfare of any kind. So the main goal of a sound immigration policy should be to make it as easy as possible for the best workers to immigrate, and impossible for the worst. Just setting a random limit doesn't help at all.
